newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends week sharply higher on technicals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends week sharply higher on technicals.

text.p: NYMEX crude ended with sharp gains Friday after a technical breakout and a thinner Brent loading schedule sparked a sizzling rally.

June crude ended 82 cents a barrel higher at $22.12 after surging as much as $1.10 to $22.40. Friday's technical breakout followed one Monday, giving prompt crude a gain of $1.69 a barrel for the week.
Refined products were swept up in crude's gains, with June gasoline ending 1.83 cents a gallon higher at 65.87 cents. June heating oil finished 1.99 cents a gallon higher at 58.87 cents.
"We have been technically strong for some time, so none of this is a surprise," said Michael Busby, dealer with Northville Industries in Melville, New York.

Chartists noted Monday's upside breakout in June crude and the proceeding sideways price action had created what has been alternatively described as a bullish pennant formation or an ascending triangle on the spot chart.

The breakout point was pinpointed around $21.55 to $21.60, also a key technical resistance area set by the high of Monday's upside reversal. After resistance was broken, a series of buy stops set by funds were triggered, dealers said.
"We have had a change in psychology in the marketplace that started when the market shrugged off bearish APIs," said Ed Kevelson, director of refined products at Paribas Futures in New York.
A thinner North Sea crude loading schedule also spurred buying as countered an oil inventory report by the American Petroleum Institute (API) Tuesday that showed burgeoning domestic crude supply.
North Sea loadings were expected to fall by about 12.50 million barrels in the shorter month of June due to maintenance programs.
"Some feel that we now have a month where we will have strong gasoline prices, and this is the start," Kevelson said.

Gasoline typically rallies during the spring in anticipation of the summer driving season when demand typically peaks. Gasoline's gains have thus far been lacklustre, and previous to this week's sharp gains, some analysts questioned whether there would be a gasoline rally this season.
Belying crude's gains, however, was a weakening June/July spread which settled in a six cent contango compared to a one cent backwardation Thursday.
Contango means the front month is less expensive than the back month and backwardation means the opposite.
"The spread has weakened which could be a disturbing signal, but it is also evidence that funds were buying since funds usually buy the back months," said Northville's Busby.
Dealers also noted the spread weakened due to position rolling from June to July ahead of the June crude contract expiry on Tuesday.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
